articleGender.example: fromage is masculine, so the article is un.

articleGenderPredicted.template: {noun} is probably {gender}: {reason} So the article would be {article}.
articleGenderPredicted.example: boulangère is probably feminine: words ending in -ère usually are. So the article would be la.

contraction.example: à + le always contracts to au.

agreementGender.hint: The adjective must agree with {noun}, which is {gender}.
agreementGender.template: The adjective must agree with {noun}, which is {gender}.
agreementGender.example: The adjective must agree with maison, which is feminine.

agreementNumber.hint: The adjective must agree with {noun}, which is {number}.
agreementNumber.template: The adjective must agree with {noun}, which is {number}.
agreementNumber.example: The adjective must agree with pommes, which is plural.

agreementGenderAndNumber.hint: The adjective must agree with {noun}, which is {gender} and {number}.
agreementGenderAndNumber.template: The adjective must agree with {noun}, which is {gender} and {number}.
agreementGenderAndNumber.example: The adjective must agree with tables, which is feminine and plural.

spelling.template: {word} isn't in the French dictionary. Did you mean {suggestion}?
spelling.example: gentile isn't in the French dictionary. Did you mean gentille?

negation.hint: In writing, “no longer” needs both ne and plus. Without ne, this reads as “more.”
negation.template: In writing, “no longer” is ne… plus: {corrected}. Without ne, this reads as “more.”
negation.example: In writing, “no longer” is ne… plus: il ne dort plus. Without ne, this reads as “more.”

idiom.hint: This is correct, but a native would usually say it another way. {note}
idiom.template: This is correct. Here's how a native would usually say it: {suggestion}. {note}
idiom.example: This is correct. Here's how a native would usually say it: bon pour la santé. For health in general, French uses the definite article.
